name: Vung Tau
provinceNote: Tourism pages and the museum still use Ba Ria–Vung Tau. Ho May and a 2026 festival report use Phường Vũng Tàu, Thành phố Hồ Chí Minh.
dotReason: Worth the night out of Ho Chi Minh City for Back Beach and the statue.
summary: A beach city on a peninsula near Ho Chi Minh City, with sandy bays and a hilltop Christ statue. Swim at Back Beach, climb to the Christ statue, ride the cable car to Ho May park, and eat banh khot, crisp mini pancakes. One or two nights suits families and weekend escapes from the city.
fee: Back Beach: no ticket. Christ the King: free.
getThere: About 100 km from Ho Chi Minh City, about two hours. About 95 km from Bien Hoa.
bestMonths: Morning swim; lunar month 8 for the whale rite
seoTitle: Vung Tau travel guide — Back Beach, the Christ statue, seafood
seoDescription: Swim on Back Beach, then the white Christ on Small Mountain. Eat bánh khọt, stingray hotpot, and the night catch on the sand. Ho Chi Minh City is about 100 km, about two hours.
intro: You wake on Back Beach to a low surf and a hotel line on the sand, with the white Christ on Small Mountain at the end of the bay and a seafood table after the swim. Stay the night if that beach, that statue, and the catch are the trip. Sleep in Ho Chi Minh City if the city is the trip, and ride down when you can give the peninsula a day.

Swim on Back Beach in the morning. The waves are fairly flat and suitable for children. Front Beach, the arc between Big Mountain and Small Mountain, is the evening walk and a drink after dark. The mistake is to photograph Mary, holding a child on Big Mountain, and caption her as the Christ. Both stand 32 metres.

Eat bánh khọt on Nguyễn Trường Tộ, one cake at a time, herbs around it and fish sauce on the side. The stingray pot, crab bánh canh, and squid hủ tiếu are the other bowls. After the swim, the night seafood market is on the same sand: you choose the fish and the cooking.
gettingAround: Ho Chi Minh City is the usual previous stop. The road is about 100 km by the Long Thanh–Ho Chi Minh City expressway, and about 95 km from Bien Hoa. Count about two hours for the ride.
Phương Trang (FUTA) and Hoa Mai are the buses. FUTA sells at the Đề Thám office. A Hoa Mai luxury ticket is 150,000 VND from 83 Nguyễn Thái Bình.

The high-speed ferry is GreenlinesDP. From 28 August 2025, Saigon boarding is Pier 4, opposite Hàm Nghi, 50 metres from the Thủ Ngư flagpole. An older note still sends you to Bến Nhà Rồng, with tickets of 120,000–250,000 VND, a landing at Front Beach, and a hydrofoil of roughly two hours. The 1 July 2026 notice lists weekday adults at 320,000 VND, down from 350,000 VND, and weekend adults at 350,000 VND; seniors 63 and over, and children 6–11, are 270,000 VND on weekdays and 300,000 VND on weekends. The booking page instead lets children under 6 ride free and uses a reduced band of ages 6–12 and over 63. Confirm the sailing time and the Vung Tau pier when you book. Weather, tide, and a technical hold can cancel a boat.

On the peninsula, a motorbike taxi can reach the Christ statue. Walk the Back Beach sand, the seafront pavement, and the hill paths to Bach Dinh and the statue. Tan Son Nhat, in Ho Chi Minh City, is the airport you use. Vung Tau has no named rail station.

stayAreas.name: Back Beach
stayAreas.summary: Beachfront hotels, restaurants, and beach clubs along the sand where you swim.

stayAreas.name: Front Beach
stayAreas.summary: The other seafront, buildings along the arc between Big Mountain and Small Mountain. The evening walk, not the main swim.

eat: Bánh khọt is the snack a Vung Tau trip turns on. Eat it on Nguyễn Trường Tộ, one cake at a time, herbs around it, sauce on the side. Then the stingray pot, crab bánh canh, squid hủ tiếu, and the Back Beach night market, where you choose the fish and the cooking.
interestsBody: Dining starts with bánh khọt, then the stingray pot, crab bánh canh, and the seafood you choose at the Back Beach night market.
Back Beach is the morning swim. Front Beach is the arc after dark.
The white statue on Small Mountain is Christ the King. Mary on Big Mountain is a different figure.

interestGroups.title: Dining and F&B
interestGroups.summary: Bánh khọt, the stingray pot, and the night catch on Back Beach.

cards.title: Dining and F&B
cards.summary: The small molded cakes on Nguyễn Trường Tộ, the stingray pot, and seafood you choose on the Back Beach sand after dark.

interestGroups.title: Back Beach morning
interestGroups.summary: The morning swim, with fairly flat waves and the hotel line on the sand.
body: Walk the sand at the start of the day, then swim, then an umbrella. The waves are fairly flat and suitable for children. Hotels, restaurants, and beach clubs line this strand.
Surf, stand-up paddle, and kite surf start from the sand. Back Beach runs 3 km.

cards.title: Back Beach
cards.summary: Surf, wet sand, and the hotel line, with the headland at the end of the bay. The morning walk and the swim.

interestGroups.title: Front Beach after dark
interestGroups.summary: The arc between the two mountains, for sunrise and a drink after dark.
body: Front Beach is the southwest arc between Big Mountain and Small Mountain. The name Tam Duong is tied to looking for the sun: sunrise is the moment, and sunset is still bright on this water. The evening is lively, with a drink after dark.
In 2026 the whale boats left this park at 5:30. That is the festival morning, not an ordinary evening.

cards.title: Front Beach
cards.summary: The curved seafront and the water. Swim on Back Beach. Come here for sunrise, or for a drink after dark.

interestGroups.title: The white statue
interestGroups.summary: Christ the King, 32 metres, on Small Mountain above Pineapple Beach.
body: The figure is Christ the King, arms out, on Small Mountain. It dates to 1974, stands 32 metres, and the climb is about 800 steps to the feet and about 100 more to the shoulders. Entry is free. A motorbike taxi can take you up if you skip the steps.

Mary on Big Mountain is also 32 metres, holding a child, and she is a different figure. The lighthouse shares this headland: one line places the tower in the early twentieth century, and another calls it the oldest lighthouse in Vietnam. Come at sunset for the view over the sea.

cards.title: Christ the King
cards.summary: Both arms, the head, and the climb. Entry is free. A motorbike taxi is the alternative to the steps.

interestGroups.title: White Villa
interestGroups.summary: Bach Dinh, started in 1898, on the Front Beach side of Big Mountain.
body: Stop at the white villa on the afternoon walk toward the Big Mountain summit. Work started in 1898. It is a late-1800s house, now a museum of local artefacts, with gardens and verandas toward the sea. The building is given as 4 Trần Phú, and the relic list as 6 Trần Phú.

One hour line is Tuesday–Friday 7:30–11:30 and 13:30–17:00, with Saturday–Sunday 7:30–17:00. Another is Tuesday–Sunday 8:00–17:00. The door is closed Monday. The French battery on the same hill still has six cannons, each about four metres and over 15 tons.

cards.title: Bach Dinh
cards.summary: The white villa and the garden stair, on the way up the hill in the afternoon.

interestGroups.title: Big Mountain
interestGroups.summary: Mary with the child, the pagoda, and the cable car. Not the Christ statue.

blocks.heading: Mary and the pagoda
paragraphs: Our Lady of Mulberry Beach is the white Mary holding the child, on the slope above Bãi Dâu. The statue was built in 1992, stands 32 metres at 60 metres above the sea, and was inaugurated on 31 December 1994. She is not Christ the King.
Thích Ca Phật Đài is the pagoda complex on Trần Phú: a seated figure, a 12 metre reclining figure, and the sculptures of Siddhartha’s life. It is a separate visit from the Christ statue.

blocks.heading: The cable car
paragraphs: Ho May’s lower station is 1A Trần Phú. The scenic ticket is the round trip and the Royal Garden viewpoint: adults 100,000 VND, children 50,000 VND. The full visit adds the rides: adults 475,000 VND, children 237,500 VND. The child price is for 1 m to 1.3 m; under 1 m is free. Park hours are 8:00–22:00. Rides are 8:00–18:00. Buy the ticket that matches the visit.

cards.title: Our Lady of Mulberry Beach
cards.summary: Mary holding the child, full figure, on Big Mountain. Also 32 metres, on a different hill from Christ.

cards.title: Thich Ca Phat Dai
cards.summary: The reclining figure and the gate on Trần Phú. A separate visit from the Christ statue.

cards.title: Ho May Park
cards.summary: A cabin toward Big Mountain. Scenic adults 100,000 VND. The full visit is 475,000 VND.

interestGroups.title: The whale rite
interestGroups.summary: Fishermen greet the whale at Thắng Tam. On an ordinary day you see the hall.
body: The communal house and the whale hall worship the whale as Nam Hải. The hall dates to the reign of Minh Mạng, 1820–1840, at 104 Hoàng Hoa Thám.

The rite is the 16th of the 8th lunar month. In 2026 the public days were 26 and 27 September, and the boats left Front Beach at 5:30. The next solar date follows the moon. Hòn Bà, the shrine rock at the end of Back Beach, is a low-tide crossing. Festival mornings there are about 5:00–9:00.

cards.title: Thang Tam whale hall
cards.summary: The whale remains in the hall on Hoàng Hoa Thám. The procession is the festival morning, not a random afternoon.

cards.title: Hon Ba
cards.summary: The shrine rock off the end of Back Beach. Cross only at low tide. Festival mornings are about 5:00–9:00.

faqs.q: Where should I swim in Vung Tau?
faqs.a: Back Beach. The waves are fairly flat and suitable for children. Front Beach is the evening walk along the arc between the two mountains, not that swim.

season.label: Whale boats at 5:30
season.note: The Nghinh Ông rite falls on the 16th of the 8th lunar month. In 2026 the public days were 26 and 27 September: boats left Front Beach at 5:30, and the next solar date follows the moon. Hòn Bà’s festival mornings are the 15th of the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th lunar months, with the low-tide walk about 5:00–9:00. GreenlinesDP does not compensate when weather, tide, a natural disaster, or a technical or security hold delays or cancels a boat.
